response:
This is a strong findings document with a stale-labeling problem of its own, and it isn't yet an executable plan. Here's my feedback in three layers: internal consistency, content, and structure/executability.

## 1. The body contradicts the status header — prune decided items

The document's whole thesis is truth-in-labeling, but the body sections have rotted behind the status paragraph:

- **P1** is titled "the one big call (owner /decide)" and lays out options (a)/(b)/(c) as open — but the header says "P1 DECIDED (ADR 0095, PR #321 open)." A reader who starts at P1 will re-litigate a settled decision.
- **P2b** asks "Decide: rename plugin vs README disambiguation" — but the header says ADR 0097 (skill-assay rename) is decided, confirmed by the owner 29-Jul, and executes last. Same problem.
- **#303** is marked "CLOSE-ready" in P2, but the header's "Remaining" list only names P2 decides for #310/#317/#302. Is #303 closed, decided, or still pending? Ambiguous.
- The **0093 anti-priming amendment** appears only in the header, with no body section explaining what "persistence implemented; --blind + separation deferred/decided" means.

Recommend restructuring around lifecycle, not discovery order: a short **Done ledger** (P0, P1, 0089, 0096, 0093-partial — one line each with the ADR/PR pointer), then **Live work only**. Decided items should not retain their argumentation sections; that's exactly the "front door makes claims the instrument has retired" defect the doc diagnoses in the repo.

## 2. Content

**What's good:** P0 is exemplary — exact file:line cites, cheap, no measurement dependency, one PR. The P2 entries carry their evidence inline (coverage 0.948–0.970, trigram 1.4–3.6% vs 0.1–0.5%, the G=10 MDE collapse for #302), which is what lets an owner /decide without re-running the investigation. Killing the $25 grid while keeping the C5 question (building-skills vs bare) is the best call in the document — it's the one live-loss condition you have.

**Gaps:**

- **The ADOPT track is the largest item and has no section.** A ~10 person-day Inspect AI substrate swap exists only as a clause in the status paragraph, while nine README lint fixes get enumerated detail. What's the adapter seam? What's kept bespoke at the boundary? What's the acceptance test that the swap didn't change verdicts on a reference benchmark? This needs its own section before its /decide, or the /decide will be under-informed.
- **The plan still mostly feeds the meta-loop.** Grok's verdict — "cleanup of the lab's conscience mistaken for product progress" — applies to the remaining list too: of everything listed, only building-skills iteration 4, the optimizing-context re-measure, and the first G≥8 batch touch lever 1, and they're sequenced last (P3, "AFTER P1 settles"). P1 has settled. So what's actually blocking iteration 4 now? If nothing, promote it to the top of the remaining list with a start condition, or the next status update will read "100% of merges went to the apparatus" again.
- **P3 is the vaguest section for the highest-stakes work.** "Char-negative reshape — iter3's own ledger names it" assumes the reader has iter3's ledger in hand. Name the target: which sections shrink, what the char budget is, what the pre-registration for the re-measure looks like.
- **"First G≥8 batch" is unscoped.** Which skills, what cost estimate, what triggers it? Given the doc's own finding that per-edit re-measures are underpowered at G=6, this batch is the mechanism that makes ADR 0095's re-measure-debt ledger honest — it deserves more than four words.
- **The /sweep section has no action.** It's a findings block ("Paired measurement QUEUED behind #317/#303"). #303's evidence is in hand — does deciding #317 unblock the sweep measurement? Say so explicitly, or move the section to the findings half.

## 3. Readability and executability

Judged against the standard of a plan a zero-context engineer could execute, this fails — deliberately, I think, because it's an owner-facing decision memo, not a task plan. That's fine, but two things follow:

- **The status paragraph is a wall.** Nine lines of comma-spliced state with parentheticals three deep. Convert to a per-item table or checkbox list (item / state / pointer). Right now the actual remaining plan is buried mid-paragraph after "Remaining:".
- **Undefined shorthand throughout:** "lever 1" (defined nowhere in the doc, only implied), "G", "rung", "route the 38 by rung", "tell-stripping blind", "0089(b)", "grok headline judge". Each needs either a one-clause gloss on first use or a pointer to where it's defined. The doc says the audit assumed a fresh reviewer; the doc itself doesn't survive one.
- **When execution starts, P0-style items convert cleanly** to bite-sized tasks (file, edit, validate.py run, commit) and the remaining decides convert to /decide agendas with the evidence block attached. The ADOPT swap is the only item that will need a real implementation plan in the full format — files, seam interfaces, test-parity criteria. Flagging that now avoids discovering it at PR time.

**Bottom line:** the findings and evidence are in good shape; the document needs one editing pass to (a) move decided items out of the argument sections, (b) give the ADOPT track and the G≥8 batch real sections, and (c) put lever-1 work first in the remaining list — since after P1's decision, the doc's own diagnosis says that's where the next unit of effort belongs.
